messages.author: e1b933a0d5bbe14f
messages.subject: [CorpLing with R] Correcting text-processed data
parts:
As we probably all know, text copied from Microsoft Word and some other programs and pasted into an ASCII text file differs from words typed there natively, particularly where apostrophes are concerned. The word "don't," for example, comes out as "don¡¯t". In the corpus I'm working with, some contributions are like this, but not all.

So is there a way we can use R to go through a corpus and replace the "corrupted" version with the intended ASCII version? Of course I could make a list of all such corrupted words and replace them all. If it were just a matter of contractions I might make the effort since this is a finite set, but this also includes the possessive form of proper nouns. Is there a one-size-fits-all approach that will find and correct all such instances?

-- 
Kevin Parent, Ph.D
VP-PR, Schoolmasters www.schoolmasters.ning.com
